summary.business_type: Local Service / Hybrid (brick-and-mortar HQ in Yerevan + service-area business across Armenia and Georgia) — Home & Construction / premium sun-shading & automation systems, official regional representative of HELLA, WAREMA, Silent Gliss
top_findings: Vercel SPA routing misconfiguration: 5 of 6 pages (/solutions, /services, /portfolio, /about, /contacts) return a genuine server-level HTTP 404 on direct fetch — the exact same request pattern Googlebot, Bingbot, AI crawlers, and real users following a shared/bookmarked link or refreshing use. Only the homepage returns 200. This is the root cause behind nearly every other finding in this audit.

Zero server-side rendering: even the one working page (the homepage) ships an empty '
' to any crawler that doesn't execute JavaScript (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot). All visible content, canonical tag, and hreflang links are injected client-side only.

raywerthi.com does not appear anywhere in Google's actual search results for any of 5 realistic target queries tested (e.g. 'HELLA официальный представитель Армения', 'Silent Gliss Армения карнизы') — unrelated businesses and foreign competitors outrank it.

LocalBusiness/Organization structured data is broken: two conflicting JSON-LD blocks give the business two different names ('Raywerthi' vs 'Raywerthi Solutions Hub') and two phone formats, and the LocalBusiness entity has no address or geo-coordinates at all despite a real office existing.

Site explicitly claims coverage of Georgia/Tbilisi but has zero supporting evidence — one Armenia-only address, one Armenian phone number, and all 8 portfolio projects tagged to Armenian cities only, undermining the claim and losing the Tbilisi-buyer search intent entirely.
quick_wins: Add a vercel.json SPA-fallback rewrite (rewrites all paths to /index.html) — a five-minute config change that unblocks 5 of 6 pages from total 404. Single highest-leverage fix on the entire audit.

Consolidate the two conflicting Organization/LocalBusiness JSON-LD blocks into one, using the real brand name 'RayWerThi' consistently, and add the missing address/geo (ready-to-use JSON-LD provided in findings/schema.md).
Add security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy) via vercel.json — currently only HSTS is present.
Fix the WhatsApp/Telegram contact buttons on /contacts, currently dead href="#" placeholders, and make the phone number a clickable tel: link.
Populate the completely empty 'Преимущества RayWerThi' (Advantages) section on the homepage — the heading exists but zero content renders underneath it.

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: robots.txt is clean, permissive, and correctly declares the sitemap
HTTPS enforced site-wide with HSTS; clean http→https and www→apex redirects
Homepage <head> has real server-delivered SEO metadata (title, description, OG/Twitter tags, static JSON-LD) before any JS runs
No accidental noindex/X-Robots-Tag blocking; no mixed content
Mobile-responsive markup with correct viewport tag; JS bundle loads without console errors

findings.title: Vercel SPA routing misconfiguration — 5 of 6 pages return real HTTP 404 on direct request
findings.description: Independently verified via curl (no JS execution, matching bot behavior) and via forced Playwright render: /solutions, /services, /portfolio, /about, /contacts all return genuine server-level 404 (X-Vercel-Error: NOT_FOUND). Only / returns 200. These are the exact URLs in sitemap.xml and the homepage nav — Google Search Console will report 'Submitted URL not found (404)' for 83% of the sitemap.
findings.recommendation: Add a vercel.json rewrite routing all non-asset paths to /index.html so React Router can handle client-side routing after initial load. Redeploy, then re-verify all 6 sitemap URLs return 200 via curl -I before resubmitting the sitemap in Search Console.

findings.title: Pure client-side rendering — canonical, hreflang, and rich structured data invisible without JS execution
findings.description:
Raw HTML for / is an empty
; canonical tag, hreflang alternates, and the richer JSON-LD @graph block are only injected client-side via react-helmet-async. Most non-Google crawlers (Bing, AI crawlers, link-preview bots, most SEO tools) rely on raw HTML and never see these signals.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to SSR/SSG (Next.js, Remix, Astro) or add a prerendering step (vite-react-ssg, Prerender.io) so canonical, hreflang, meta description, and title exist in raw HTML for every route. Minimum viable interim fix: move the homepage's canonical/hreflang into the static index.html <head>.

findings.title: hreflang alternates all point to the identical URL — HY/EN content is not indexable
findings.description: All four hreflang values (ru, hy, en, x-default) resolve to the same URL. The RU/HY/EN switcher is three buttons with no href/path prefix — pure client-side state, confirmed no i18n routing pattern in the production bundle.
findings.recommendation: Re-architect the language switcher to produce real, distinct, crawlable URLs per language (e.g. /en/solutions, /hy/solutions) with correct reciprocal hreflang, each with its own title/meta description. Only then add hreflang entries to the sitemap.

findings.title: Missing critical security headers
findings.description: Only Strict-Transport-Security is present on responses. CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are all absent — a real security gap for a site collecting lead/contact data.
findings.recommendation: Add security headers via vercel.json headers config. Test CSP in report-only mode first since the app loads Google Fonts and Unsplash-hosted images.

findings.title: Oversized, non-responsive LCP-candidate images
findings.description: Hero image is a single 1920x1080, 250KB JPEG served identically to all breakpoints with no srcset/sizes and no modern format. Header logo is a 116KB PNG rendered at 25x more pixel data than needed, no width/height attributes.
findings.recommendation: Generate responsive srcset/sizes variants, convert to WebP/AVIF, add explicit width/height, and preload the hero image with fetchpriority="high".

findings.title: Render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet with no preconnect
findings.description: Google Fonts CSS loads synchronously with no preconnect/dns-prefetch hints, adding avoidable latency to FCP/LCP; six font weights requested for one family.
findings.recommendation: Add preconnect hints for fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com, trim requested font weights, or self-host Inter via @fontsource/inter.

findings.title: Duplicate, inconsistent Organization structured data
findings.description: Two JSON-LD Organization blocks with different names ('Raywerthi' static vs 'Raywerthi Solutions Hub' client-injected) and different phone formats coexist on the homepage.
findings.recommendation: Keep one JSON-LD source of truth with a consistent business name and phone format across schema, title tag, and Google Business Profile listing.

findings.title: www→apex redirect uses temporary (307) instead of permanent status
findings.description: https://www.raywerthi.com/ redirects with 307 instead of 301/308, making link-equity consolidation less certain.
findings.recommendation: Change the www→apex redirect to a permanent status code (301/308) at the DNS/domain config level.

findings.title: IndexNow protocol not implemented
findings.description: No IndexNow key file or API calls found — Bing/Yandex/Naver support near-instant crawl notification on publish/update.
findings.recommendation: Low priority until the routing fix ships. Once fixed, generate an IndexNow key and submit the 6 sitemap URLs to accelerate re-crawl.

findings.title: Minimal favicon/touch-icon set
findings.description: Only a single .ico favicon; no apple-touch-icon, SVG favicon, or web app manifest.
findings.recommendation: Add a modern icon set (favicon.svg, apple-touch-icon.png, site.webmanifest) — low priority polish item.

categories.name: Sitemap & Crawl Coverage
what_works: sitemap.xml is valid, well-formed XML correctly declared in robots.txt
6 URLs are well within Google's limits; no orphaned/extraneous entries
Domain canonicalization (http→https, www→apex) is correctly handled at the edge

findings.title: 5 of 6 sitemap URLs return HTTP 404 on the exact request pattern Googlebot uses to verify sitemap entries
findings.description: Same root cause as the technical-SEO routing finding — restated here because it means the sitemap is actively telling Google to index 5 URLs that 404. Retested 3 times with a Googlebot user-agent string, same result.
findings.recommendation: Same fix as technical finding #1 (vercel.json SPA rewrite). Re-verify all 6 URLs return 200 before resubmitting in Search Console.

findings.title: No lastmod on any of the 6 URL entries
findings.description: None of the 6 <url> entries include a <lastmod> tag, giving Google no freshness signal at all.
findings.recommendation: Add lastmod in YYYY-MM-DD format reflecting genuine content-change dates per route, not a uniform build-time stamp.

findings.title: Deprecated priority/changefreq tags present
findings.description: Every entry sets priority and changefreq, both of which Google has stated are ignored for ranking/crawl purposes.
findings.recommendation: Optional cleanup — safe to remove, no ranking impact either way.

categories.name: Content Quality (E-E-A-T)
what_works: Legitimate authority hook: official representative of three recognized international manufacturers (HELLA, WAREMA, Silent Gliss)
Genuine multi-market, multi-language targeting (RU/HY/EN) reflecting real audience needs
Niche vertical focus with genuine case-study/differentiation potential
Homepage is reachable and indexable, giving at least one crawlable entry point

findings.title: Five of six pages return HTTP 404 — content is effectively unindexed regardless of quality
findings.description: A page search engines record as 404 will not be indexed or ranked no matter how strong its underlying content is. This is the dominant factor suppressing the content score.
findings.recommendation: Fix the Vercel routing issue first — nearly every other content finding is provisional until then.

findings.title: Trustworthiness signals unverified — highest-weighted E-E-A-T factor is the biggest blind spot
findings.description: Trust (30% of E-E-A-T weight) depends heavily on /contacts and /about, precisely the pages that 404. Physical address, manufacturer-authorization proof, and legal entity details could not be confirmed as reachable content.
findings.recommendation: Once routing is fixed, verify /contacts shows a real address and phone numbers for both markets, and /about publishes visible proof of manufacturer authorization with verifiable partner-page links.

findings.title: Expertise/experience signals (staff credentials, real case studies) unconfirmed
findings.description: No named staff/installer credentials, certifications, or detailed project case studies with real photos/specs could be confirmed on /portfolio or /services.
findings.recommendation: Once accessible, add real project photography, address/region tags per project, named team members, and concrete differentiators (warranty terms, completed-installation counts).

findings.title: Word-count/topical-coverage floors not confirmed against page-type minimums
findings.description: Insufficient data gathered for /solutions, /services, /portfolio, /about, /contacts before the audit's data-gathering turns were exhausted — flagged for re-audit rather than guessed.
findings.recommendation: Re-run word-count and topical-coverage extraction once the routing fix is deployed and pages reliably return 200.

findings.title: Homepage readability and freshness signals not fully captured
findings.description: Insufficient data gathered on exact word count, keyword density, and freshness metadata for the homepage — flagged for re-audit.
findings.recommendation: Re-fetch and run full readability and freshness checks on the homepage.

findings.title: Risk of templated/repetitive structure across RU/HY/EN variants unverified
findings.description: Could not confirm whether language variants are genuinely localized versus straight machine-translated strings.
findings.recommendation: Compare corresponding sections across all three locales for genuine localization once real per-language URLs exist.

findings.title: AI citation readiness could not be assessed
findings.description: Structured data completeness, heading hierarchy, and quotable/extractable facts across the site were not fully assessed due to the routing blocker.
findings.recommendation: Once routing is fixed, ensure clear H1-H6 hierarchy and add quotable factual statements (e.g. 'authorized dealer since YYYY').

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: Homepage ships valid, server-rendered JSON-LD (Organization + LocalBusiness) with correct @context and absolute URLs
areaServed (Armenia, Georgia, Caucasus) present on both entities
No deprecated schema types in use
priceRange set on LocalBusiness

findings.title: Inner pages return HTTP 404 — all schema on them is currently unreachable by crawlers
findings.description: JS-rendered snapshots show full page-specific schema exists on /solutions, /services, /portfolio, but a plain HTTP GET (how Googlebot's initial crawl and schema-validation tools fetch a URL) receives a 404 first, so none of it has any rich-result eligibility today.
findings.recommendation: Fix the Vercel SPA rewrite so all routes serve 200. Re-fetch each URL raw (no JS) and confirm 200 before treating any schema on those pages as valid.

findings.title: LocalBusiness entity is missing address entirely
findings.description: No PostalAddress or geo property at all despite a real, visible street address existing in the rendered HTML — a core property for local search eligibility.
findings.recommendation: Add a PostalAddress with streetAddress, addressLocality, and addressCountry, plus GeoCoordinates. Verify the exact address from /contacts once reachable.

findings.title: Duplicate, conflicting Organization schema on the homepage
findings.description: Two Organization JSON-LD blocks disagree on business name ('Raywerthi' vs 'Raywerthi Solutions Hub' — neither exactly matches the visible brand 'RayWerThi') and phone formatting.
findings.recommendation: Remove the duplicate static block; standardize name to match the visible brand and use one consistent E.164 phone format. Ready-to-use consolidated JSON-LD provided in findings/schema.md.

findings.title: Generic LocalBusiness type instead of a more specific valid subtype
findings.description: The business maps well to HomeAndConstructionBusiness, a Google-recognized LocalBusiness subtype, but uses the generic type.
findings.recommendation: Use ["LocalBusiness", "HomeAndConstructionBusiness"] as the @type.

findings.title: Missing logo, sameAs, email, and contactPoint properties
findings.description: Neither JSON-LD block includes a logo URL, social/GBP sameAs links, the real contact email, or a ContactPoint with availableLanguage despite the site supporting RU/HY/EN.
findings.recommendation: Add these properties to the consolidated Organization node — full example provided in findings/schema.md.

findings.title: No WebSite or BreadcrumbList schema anywhere
findings.description: No WebSite entity tying Organization/LocalBusiness together, and no BreadcrumbList despite a clear site hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Add a WebSite node with publisher linking to Organization, and per-page BreadcrumbList once inner pages return 200.

findings.title: No Service/Product schema despite six distinct offerings described on /solutions
findings.description: Six offerings tied to specific brands are described but not expressed as Service/Product schema. Low priority until the page itself is indexable.
findings.recommendation: Once routing is fixed, add one Service entity per solution category with provider, areaServed, and brand.

findings.title: Address/contact details unverified pending routing fix
findings.description: Because /contacts 404s on raw fetch, exact street address, opening hours, and geo coordinates could not be confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Once /contacts is reachable, pull authoritative address/hours and replace placeholders before publishing new schema.

categories.name: Performance (Core Web Vitals)
what_works: Hero image has explicit width/height attributes, reducing CLS risk
Below-the-fold images use loading="lazy" consistently
Single CSS/JS Vite production build output, no duplicate bundle shipping
Inline SVG icons rather than icon fonts or sprites
Homepage DOM size (~340 tags) is well under the INP-risk threshold

findings.title: 5 of 6 primary routes are unreachable, blocking all real-world CWV measurement
findings.description: A URL that 404s on direct load/reload cannot be said to meet Core Web Vitals in the field regardless of underlying SPA speed, since real users landing directly see a failed load, not a slow one. No PSI/CrUX/Lighthouse data could be captured for this audit at all (rate-limited/tooling failure) — every score here is a conservative, explicitly-labeled estimate, not a measurement.
findings.recommendation: Fix the SPA routing issue first — a precondition for any real CWV measurement. Then run PSI/Lighthouse/CrUX against all 6 URLs to replace every estimate in this category with real numbers.

findings.title: Single monolithic JS bundle for a dependency-heavy 6-page site (estimated INP/LCP risk)
findings.description: No evidence of route-based code-splitting; package.json lists ~25 Radix UI packages, recharts, embla-carousel, and other libraries that may not all be used, all shipped in one bundle to every visitor.
findings.recommendation: Audit and remove unused dependencies, enable route-based code splitting via React.lazy()/dynamic import per page, and inspect real chunk sizes via a production vite build.

findings.title: Portfolio preview images hotlinked from Unsplash without explicit dimensions
findings.description: 6 homepage project images load from images.unsplash.com with loading="lazy" but no width/height attributes, a CLS/LCP risk, plus an unnecessary third-party dependency.
findings.recommendation: Self-host and optimize portfolio images (WebP/AVIF, responsive srcset) with explicit dimensions on every image.

findings.title: No preconnect/preload/dns-prefetch resource hints
findings.description: No resource hints for the likely LCP hero image or third-party image/font origins.
findings.recommendation: Add preload for the hero image and preconnect for any retained third-party origins.

findings.title: Web font loading strategy unknown
findings.description: No font declarations found in rendered HTML head — fonts may be bundled in CSS (not fetched in this audit) or the site may use system fonts.
findings.recommendation: Confirm via the built CSS file; if web fonts are used, ensure font-display: swap and preload the primary file.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: robots.txt does not block AI crawlers — falls through to a permissive wildcard Allow: / group
A static, JS-independent JSON-LD Organization block exists in the raw head, readable by non-rendering crawlers
Static title and meta description are present and descriptive on the raw homepage HTML
Once rendered, content is on-topic and unambiguous about brand, partnerships, and service area

findings.title: 5 of 6 pages return genuine HTTP 404 to every crawler that doesn't execute JavaScript — including essentially all major AI crawlers
findings.description: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot, and CCBot are all documented as non-JS-executing. The 404 is a genuine server-side response reproduced even under forced full-browser rendering — no client-side router ever gets a chance to run for these paths.
findings.recommendation: Same P0 fix as technical/sitemap findings: add the Vercel SPA rewrite. Every other GEO recommendation is moot for 5 of 6 pages until this lands.

findings.title: Raw (non-JS) HTML for every page is an empty shell with zero body text for any non-rendering AI crawler
findings.description: The entire site's independently-fetchable text budget for a non-rendering crawler is a meta description (~30 words) and one static JSON-LD block. Even the JS-rendered homepage carries only 167 words of extractable body text total.
findings.recommendation: Implement SSR, static pre-rendering, or a bot-triggered prerender layer so the first HTTP response for every URL contains full readable text. The single highest-leverage fix in this audit for citability, structural readability, and technical accessibility simultaneously.

findings.title: llms.txt does not exist
findings.description: /llms.txt returns 404. No explicit crawler-friendly summary of the business and its pages exists to partially compensate for the CSR content-access problem.
findings.recommendation: Create /llms.txt with a concise summary of the company, links to core pages, and contact info — low effort, though value is gated behind the routing/SSR fixes.

findings.title: robots.txt does not explicitly name any AI crawler — relies entirely on wildcard fallthrough
findings.description: No dedicated groups for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc. — currently allowed only implicitly via the wildcard, which is fragile to future edits.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit Allow: / groups for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot for documentation and future-proofing.

findings.title: Duplicate, mutually inconsistent JSON-LD and meta description tags in the rendered head
findings.description: react-helmet-async appends rather than replaces the static Organization block and meta description, so two versions of each exist simultaneously with different wording/names.
findings.recommendation: Fix react-helmet-async to replace static placeholders rather than append; standardize on one canonical name and description everywhere.

findings.title: Zero brand/entity corroboration signals anywhere on-site
findings.description: No social links (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn), no reviews/testimonials markup, and minimal case-study detail — no cross-corroboration pathway for AI systems to validate the business.
findings.recommendation: Add functioning social/GBP links with sameAs entries in schema; even a small install/process video on YouTube is the strongest documented correlate with AI citation.

findings.title: No FAQ-style, question-based, or comparison content anywhere
findings.description: All headings are declarative, not question-phrased; no FAQPage schema; the 'Преимущества RayWerThi' section renders completely empty despite being the natural home for citable differentiators.
findings.recommendation: Add a short FAQ section covering brand representation, service areas, and process; fix the empty Advantages section first since it's already structurally planned for this content.

findings.title: Multi-language content exists only as client-side UI state — HY/EN invisible to all crawlers
findings.description: Cross-referenced from the technical/sitemap hreflang finding, restated for its direct GEO impact — two of three target-language audiences currently cannot be reached via AI search at all.
findings.recommendation: Implement real per-language routing once SSR and the routing fix are in place.

categories.name: Local SEO
what_works: areaServed (Armenia, Georgia, Caucasus) is machine-readably declared, even if not backed by location pages
Phone number digits are consistent everywhere they appear, only formatting differs
A Google Maps iframe and real street address exist on /contacts
Multiple contact channels offered (phone, email, WhatsApp, Telegram) reflecting regional client preferences
Portfolio cards carry a location tag, showing the template supports location-tagged proof of work

findings.title: /contacts and /about — the only pages carrying NAP and Georgia-market claims — return real HTTP 404
findings.description: The entire local-NAP payload of the site (address, phone, map, lead form, official-representative claims) exists only behind the same routing bug documented elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Same fix as the site-wide routing issue; re-verify these two URLs return 200 before any further local-SEO work.

findings.title: LocalBusiness schema has no address or geo despite a real visible office
findings.description: Cross-referenced from the schema audit — directly undercuts Local Pack and Knowledge Panel eligibility.
findings.recommendation: Add PostalAddress and GeoCoordinates to the LocalBusiness entity.

findings.title: Conflicting business name and phone formatting across two simultaneous JSON-LD blocks
findings.description: The business name appears in three different forms across the site (RayWerThi, Raywerthi, Raywerthi Solutions Hub) — a documented ranking suppressor when it mismatches the Google Business Profile listing.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on one canonical name and phone format everywhere, including the GBP listing itself.

findings.title: No verifiable Google Business Profile signal
findings.description: The Maps embed uses a generic text-search query, not a Place ID/CID — proves nothing about a claimed/verified GBP listing. No reviews, ratings, or photo carousel found anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether a GBP listing exists and is claimed; replace the embed with a real Place ID reference once available.

findings.title: Zero reviews, testimonials, or ratings anywhere on the site
findings.description: No aggregateRating or Review schema, no visible testimonials — a significant trust gap for a premium-positioned installer.
findings.recommendation: Actively solicit reviews post-installation and surface a review widget with aggregateRating schema.

findings.title: Site claims two-country footprint (Armenia + Georgia) but has zero Georgia-tagged proof of work
findings.description: All 5-8 portfolio projects are tagged to Armenian cities only; no Georgia address, phone, or case study exists despite explicit 'successful projects in Georgia' copy.
findings.recommendation: Add at least one real Georgia/Tbilisi project with photos and city tag, or soften the claim until evidence exists — an unsupported claim damages trust more than a modest one.

findings.title: Visible NAP address block omits city name and postal code
findings.description: The visible address widget shows only country and street, not city — undermining citation-matching consistency.
findings.recommendation: Complete the visible address to full 'Street, City, Country' format.

findings.title: Armenian-language toggle produces no independently crawlable Armenian content
findings.description: Cross-referenced from the hreflang finding — a missed local-trust signal for the home-market Armenian-speaking audience.
findings.recommendation: Implement real per-language URLs once SSR/routing fixes are in place.

findings.title: WhatsApp and Telegram contact buttons are non-functional href="#" placeholders
findings.description: Both messaging-app buttons on /contacts link nowhere, directly reducing lead capture from the region's preferred first-contact channels.
findings.recommendation: Wire both buttons to real wa.me/t.me deep links.

findings.title: Contact email uses a free Gmail address rather than the owned domain
findings.description: All mailto: links point to a Gmail address despite owning raywerthi.com.
findings.recommendation: Set up and switch to a branded domain email address.

findings.title: LocalBusiness uses the generic type with no openingHoursSpecification
findings.description: Cross-referenced from the schema audit — a completeness gap once address/geo are added.
findings.recommendation: Add HomeAndConstructionBusiness subtype and openingHoursSpecification.

categories.name: Search Experience (SXO)
what_works: Homepage hero has a single, clear value proposition with two well-differentiated CTAs
/services and /solutions content (verified via rendered HTML) map well to what SERP consensus rewards for their page types
/contacts has a real geocoded map, working lead form, and three parallel contact channels
Portfolio grid has the right data shape (city + product/brand tag per project), even though depth is currently shallow
robots.txt allows all crawlers — the 404s are a routing config gap, not a deliberate exclusion, making this a fixable architecture problem

findings.title: Site does not appear in Google search results for any of 5 realistic target queries tested
findings.description: Live search checks for queries like 'HELLA официальный представитель Армения' and 'Silent Gliss Армения карнизы' show zero appearances of raywerthi.com — competitors, generic catalogs, and even an unrelated automotive-parts business outrank it. Directly explained by the crawl/index failure documented across this audit.
findings.recommendation: P0, fix the routing issue — this is the precondition for any SXO improvement to matter in search at all.

findings.title: Site architecture collapses 5 distinct search intents into 1 crawlable URL, while the SERP rewards per-intent pages
findings.description: SERP consensus across all 5 queries is dominated by narrow-intent pages (local directory, product catalog, distributor page). RayWerThi's content model matches this shape in principle but Google can currently only index the single combined homepage.
findings.recommendation: After the routing fix, extend the architecture with intent-specific pages — a Georgia/Tbilisi-focused page and per-brand/category landing pages.

findings.title: 'Преимущества RayWerThi' (Advantages) section renders completely empty
findings.description: A full heading exists with a zero-child content container beneath it — exactly the section that should carry the strongest Authority/Trust signals.
findings.recommendation: Investigate the broken data source/render call and populate with 3-6 concrete advantage cards (years in business, warranty, direct manufacturer supply).

findings.title: 'HELLA' brand-name entity collision suppresses branded-distributor visibility
findings.description: Searching for HELLA's official Armenia representative surfaces an unrelated automotive-parts retailer sharing the same trademark, competing for the same search real estate.
findings.recommendation: Consistently pair 'HELLA' with shading-specific terms in titles/H1s/schema, and consider explicit disambiguation copy once indexed.

findings.title: Portfolio uses generic stock photography, not real project photos, on a page claiming 'Реализованные объекты'
findings.description: All 8 portfolio images resolve to Unsplash stock URLs despite specific-sounding project names — a credibility risk if noticed by a Decision-stage buyer.
findings.recommendation: Replace with real, self-hosted project photography as projects are completed.

findings.title: No pricing, spec sheets, or downloadable technical content for evaluators
findings.description: No price ranges or named smart-home protocols beyond a generic mention, while competing content goes further into product specifics.
findings.recommendation: Add starting-price indicators and name specific supported smart-home platforms; consider a downloadable spec-sheet PDF per brand.

findings.title: No testimonials, reviews, or third-party trust signals anywhere
findings.description: The single lowest-scoring dimension across all 5 tested personas (Trust: 6-9/25 for every persona).
findings.recommendation: Collect and publish real client testimonials tied to specific projects; pursue Google Business Profile reviews.

findings.title: Contact phone number is not a clickable tel: link
findings.description: Appears as plain text sitewide, adding friction to the lowest-friction possible mobile conversion action.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the phone number in an href="tel:..." link sitewide.

categories.name: Visual & Mobile
what_works: Homepage design is visually strong: polished hero, clear value proposition, dual CTAs above the fold on both breakpoints
Mobile layout reflows cleanly to a single column with no visible overlap or text cutoff
Brand/partner logo section reads clearly at both breakpoints, reinforcing credibility

findings.title: Primary navigation destinations return a Vercel 404 error page on every device
findings.description: Screenshots of /solutions, /services, /portfolio, /contacts on both desktop and mobile show a plain Vercel '404: NOT_FOUND' error card, not site content — confirmed both by file-size analysis (error pages are ~13-21KB vs 1-2.9MB for the real homepage) and by visually opening the images.
findings.recommendation: Same routing fix as the rest of this audit; re-capture screenshots to confirm before any further visual QA on these templates.

findings.title: Cannot verify above-the-fold and responsiveness for 4 of 5 templates
findings.description: Because the affected pages are error pages, no standard visual QA (CTA placement, layout shift, touch-target sizing) could be evaluated for them.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the full screenshot capture and visual QA pass across all breakpoints once routing is fixed.

findings.title: Mobile header appears to lack a visible hamburger/menu control

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Add a vercel.json SPA-fallback rewrite so /solutions, /services, /portfolio, /about, /contacts all serve the app (200) instead of a platform 404 — the single highest-leverage fix on the entire audit
Re-verify all 6 sitemap URLs return 200 via curl -I, then resubmit sitemap.xml in Google Search Console and request re-indexing

Consolidate the two conflicting Organization/LocalBusiness JSON-LD blocks into one, standardized on the real brand name 'RayWerThi' with one phone format, and add the missing PostalAddress + GeoCoordinates (ready-to-use JSON-LD in findings/schema.md)
Add security headers (CSP report-only to start, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy) via vercel.json

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Implement SSR/pre-rendering (or at minimum move canonical/hreflang/meta tags into static index.html) so raw HTML contains real content for every route — unlocks AI-search visibility and non-Google crawler indexing
Re-architect the RU/HY/EN language switcher to produce real, distinct, crawlable URLs with correct reciprocal hreflang
Populate the empty 'Преимущества RayWerThi' section with 3-6 concrete advantage cards
Fix the WhatsApp/Telegram href="#" placeholder links and make the phone number a clickable tel: link sitewide
Add real Georgia/Tbilisi proof (address, phone, or at least one tagged portfolio project) or soften the unsupported Georgia coverage claim
Confirm or create/claim a Google Business Profile listing; replace the generic Maps query embed with a real Place ID embed once available
Optimize the hero image and logo (responsive srcset, WebP/AVIF, explicit dimensions, preload)
Verify a working mobile hamburger menu exists — currently unconfirmed from screenshots

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Add a short FAQ section covering brand representation, service areas, and process, with FAQPage schema
Replace stock Unsplash portfolio photography with real, self-hosted project photos
Collect and publish real client testimonials with aggregateRating schema; pursue Google Business Profile reviews
Add /llms.txt with a concise business summary and links to core pages
Reach out to HELLA, WAREMA, and Silent Gliss for hyperlinked dealer-locator listings
Register free Moz and Bing Webmaster Tools accounts for ongoing backlink visibility
Add starting-price indicators and named smart-home platform support for technical evaluators

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Re-run PageSpeed Insights/Lighthouse/CrUX against all 6 URLs once routing is fixed to replace every performance estimate with real measurements
Monitor Google Search Console indexing status weekly until all 6 pages show as indexed
Track SERP rankings for the 5 target queries tested in this audit as a leading indicator of recovery
Re-run the backlink audit in 3-6 months once Moz/Bing data is available
Re-audit content quality and word-count/topical-coverage once inner pages are reliably reachable
